stem: The rate of inventory turnover is calculated as …

options.rationale: Correct: the syllabus formula.
Inventory is at cost, so it is compared with cost of sales, not revenue.
The formula uses average inventory.
This mixes the inventory days formula with revenue.

explanation: Rate of inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory, where average = (opening + closing) ÷ 2.

stem: Cost of sales was US\$54,600. Inventory was US\$7,200 at the start of the year and US\$8,400 at the end. What was the rate of inventory turnover?

options.rationale: Closing inventory has been used instead of average inventory.
Opening inventory has been used instead of average inventory.
Opening and closing inventory have been added but not divided by 2.

stem: Trade receivables are US\$6,300 and credit sales for the year were US\$46,000. What is the trade receivables turnover in days (to the nearest day)?

options.rationale: The fraction has been turned upside down.
This multiplies by 52 (weeks), not 365.
This multiplies by 100, giving a percentage, not days.

stem: Trade payables are US\$5,840. Purchases for the year were US\$43,200, of which US\$4,800 were cash purchases. What is the trade payables turnover in days (to the nearest day)?

options.rationale: Total purchases have been used; cash purchases never create a trade payable.
Cash purchases have been deducted twice.
This multiplies by 12, which would give months, not days.

stem: A trader's rate of inventory turnover fell from 9 times to 6 times a year. What does this most likely mean?

options.rationale: That would raise the rate.

options.content: Goods are taking longer to sell
options.rationale: Correct: inventory is replaced fewer times a year.
That is shown by trade receivables days.

options.content: The gross profit margin has risen
options.rationale: Inventory turnover measures speed of sale, not margin.

explanation: A lower rate means average inventory is sold fewer times: goods stay on the shelves longer.

stem: A business allows customers 30 days' credit. Its trade receivables turnover is 52 days. Which action would most directly improve this?

options.content: Taking longer to pay its own suppliers
options.rationale: This affects payables days, not receivables days.
This affects inventory turnover.
This does not make customers pay faster.

options.content: Offering a discount for prompt payment
options.rationale: Correct: it encourages customers to pay sooner.

explanation: Receivables days fall when customers pay faster: cash discounts, prompt invoicing and chasing overdue accounts all help.

stem: Trade payables turnover has risen from 35 days to 75 days while suppliers allow 45 days. What is the main risk?

options.rationale: This relates to inventory turnover.

options.content: Customers will stop paying on time
options.rationale: Customers' payments are not affected by when the business pays its suppliers.

options.content: The gross profit margin will rise
options.rationale: Delaying payment does not change buying or selling prices.
Correct: the business is paying well outside the agreed terms.

explanation: Paying late keeps cash in the business for a while but damages goodwill with suppliers, who may stop giving credit.
hints: Compare the payment period with the credit period allowed.

stem: Average inventory is US\$10,000 and cost of sales US\$73,000. What is the inventory turnover in days?

options.rationale: This is roughly the rate in times (7.3), not days.
The fraction has been inverted before multiplying by 365.

explanation: Inventory days = average inventory ÷ cost of sales × 365 = 50 days (or 365 ÷ 7.3 times).

stem: Inventory turnover uses cost of sales rather than revenue because inventory is valued at cost.
explanation: True. Comparing a cost figure with a selling-price figure would overstate the rate.

stem: Cash sales should be included in the sales figure used to calculate trade receivables days.
explanation: False. Only credit sales create trade receivables, so the formula uses credit sales.

stem: Match each ratio with its formula.
explanation: The 'times' ratio has cost of sales on top; the 'days' ratios have the balance on top and multiply by 365.
Average inventory is the simple average of the opening and closing figures.

stem: Inventory at 1 January 2025 was US\$11,650 and at 31 December 2025 US\$13,350. Cost of sales was US\$88,750. Calculate the rate of inventory turnover, to one decimal place.
explanation: Average = (11,650 + 13,350) ÷ 2 = 12,500. 88,750 ÷ 12,500 = 7.1 times. Using closing inventory gives 6.6.
workedSolution: 1. Average = (11,650 + 13,350) ÷ 2 = 12,500. 88,750 ÷ 12,500 = 7.1 times. Using closing inventory gives 6.6.

stem: Farai's revenue was US\$96,000; he sells at a mark-up of 25%. Inventory was US\$9,400 at the start of the year and US\$10,800 at the end. Calculate his rate of inventory turnover, to one decimal place.
explanation: Cost of sales = 96,000 × 100/125 = 76,800. Average inventory = 10,100. Turnover = 7.6 times. Using revenue gives 9.5; treating 25% as a margin gives 7.1.
workedSolution: 1. Cost of sales = 96,000 × 100/125 = 76,800. Average inventory = 10,100. Turnover = 7.6 times. Using revenue gives 9.5; treating 25% as a margin gives 7.1.
hints: Find cost of sales from the mark-up first: revenue × 100/125.

stem: Chipo's total sales were US\$71,400, of which US\$12,500 were cash sales. Trade receivables at the year end were US\$8,920. Calculate her trade receivables turnover in days, to the nearest whole day.
explanation: Credit sales = 71,400 − 12,500 = 58,900. 8,920 ÷ 58,900 × 365 = 55.3 → 55 days. Using total sales gives 46 days.
workedSolution: 1. Credit sales = 71,400 − 12,500 = 58,900. 8,920 ÷ 58,900 × 365 = 55.3 → 55 days. Using total sales gives 46 days.

stem: Give **two** ways a shop could increase its rate of inventory turnover.

points.description: Buy smaller quantities more often / hold less inventory
Clear slow-moving or old lines (sales, promotions) / stock only goods that sell well / advertise to increase sales

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Order smaller amounts more often so less inventory is held, and clear slow-selling lines with a sale.

explanation: Either reduce average inventory or increase cost of sales (sell more).

stem: Sipho collects from customers in 25 days and pays his suppliers in 60 days. His suppliers allow 30 days. Evaluate this position.

points.description: Positive: cash comes in long before it goes out, helping liquidity
Negative: paying 30 days late breaks suppliers' terms; risk of losing credit, discounts or goodwill
Conclusion: he should move towards paying within 30 days while keeping his good collection period

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Collecting in 25 days but paying in 60 means he holds the cash for a long time, which helps his bank balance. But he is paying twice as slowly as his suppliers allow, so they may stop his credit or charge more. He should pay within the 30 days and still keep a comfortable cash position because his customers pay quickly.

explanation: A balanced answer weighs liquidity against supplier goodwill.
hints: Consider both the cash benefit and the supplier relationship.

stem:
Tendai Mupfumi sells hardware to builders on credit in Harare. He allows customers 30 days and his suppliers allow him 30 days. Figures for 2025:

| Item for 2025 | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Credit sales | 128,500 |
| Cost of sales | 112,420 |
| Credit purchases | 113,900 |
| Inventory at 1 January 2025 | 14,600 |
| Inventory at 31 December 2025 | 16,200 |
| Trade receivables at 31 December 2025 | 15,840 |
| Trade payables at 31 December 2025 | 8,420 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the rate of inventory turnover, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the inventory turnover in days, to the nearest whole day.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the trade receivables turnover in days, to the nearest whole day.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the trade payables turnover in days, to the nearest whole day.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Comment on Tendai's management of receivables and payables, and advise him.

points.description: Customers take about 45 days against 30 allowed: credit control is weak
He pays suppliers in about 27 days, within their 30 days
Advice: chase debts / offer cash discounts / vet customers, so that he does not pay out cash before he collects it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Customers take about 45 days to pay although they are allowed 30, so his credit control is weak. He pays his suppliers in about 27 days, within their terms, so he is paying out cash well before he collects it. He should chase overdue accounts and offer a small discount for payment within 30 days.

parts.explanation: Compare each period with the terms.

explanation: Inventory turnover 7.3 times (50 days); receivables 45 days; payables 27 days.
hints: Use average inventory with cost of sales.

stem:
Rudo Makoni sells shoes in Gweru. Figures for two years:

|  | 2024 US\$ | 2025 US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cost of sales | 46,800 | 49,950 |
| Opening inventory | 5,400 | 6,600 |
| Closing inventory | 6,600 | 9,050 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the rate of inventory turnover for 2024, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the rate of inventory turnover for 2025, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which statement best describes the change?

options.content: Shoes are selling faster because cost of sales has increased this year
options.rationale: The rate fell, so goods sell more slowly.

options.content: The gross profit margin has fallen because inventory is higher
options.rationale: Inventory turnover gives no information about the margin.

options.content: Shoes are selling more slowly as inventory grew faster than sales
options.rationale: Correct: closing inventory rose by about 37% while cost of sales rose by under 7%.

options.content: Customers are taking longer to pay for the shoes they buy
options.rationale: Inventory turnover does not measure customer payments.

parts.explanation: The rate fell from 7.8 to 6.4 times.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain **two** problems caused by a falling rate of inventory turnover and suggest **one** remedy.

points.description: Money tied up in inventory, so less cash for paying debts (worse liquidity)
Risk of goods going out of fashion, damage or theft; higher storage/insurance costs
Remedy: buy smaller quantities more often / clearance sale of slow lines

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cash is tied up in shoes on the shelves, so there is less to pay suppliers; and older styles may go out of fashion and have to be sold below cost. Rudo should order smaller quantities more often and hold a sale to clear slow lines.

parts.explanation: Two problems plus one practical remedy.
